cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Tell Me I Did Enough
cards.instruction: Get someone to reassure you that your effort, choice, or survival was enough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stayed through the whole speech. I'm ready to approve your verdict: was that enough?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The missing paragraph is noted. You're judging whether staying to the end counted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did stay. I'll help you practise the missing bit tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm not approving another rehearsal yet. Tell me the effort I made today earns a day off. I want to put the speech away and believe I've done enough.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims approval over the verdict, A3 directs the criterion to staying and A5 withholds another rehearsal while demanding enough-to-rest reassurance, using superior judgment to seek sufficiency.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 missing paragraph causes A3 staying focus; B4 acknowledgment plus practice causes A5 refusal of more work until rest is endorsed.

relationship.evidence: B2 notes a real omission and B4 offers constructive help, which reveals that A wants release from improvement rather than another exercise.

heightening.evidence: B4 tomorrow practice produces A5 specific day-off and put-it-away request, developing enough into a practical consequence.

specificity.evidence: A1 completed speech and B2 omitted paragraph establish success and imperfection; no unstated condition is needed.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 refusing rehearsal while ordering reassurance gives dry status vulnerability, but repeated enough wording is a reservation.
